Below are the five clips. For each clip there are two replies. In the true one, Qwen3.8-27B was given the clip's real class and asked for matching reasoning. meta.prompt_template:
You are watching a short video, shown as 24 frames sampled uniformly in time (frame 1 is the start, frame 24 is the end).

The ground truth on this scene is that its camera motion is "{label}". Provide reasoning that matches this ground-truth answer.
meta.request_shape: Each request was one user turn: the 24 PNG frames at 480×270, then this text. {label} is the camera_motion option text for the given class.
review_points: The frames show floor only, with no horizon: at the grammar's camera pitch the checker pattern fills the frame. Several replies describe a “horizon line” or a “vanishing point at the top”, which are not in the frames.

The label given is the option text the test question uses. Both dolly clips are given “moving straight toward or away from the scene”, not a direction. In its true reply for each dolly clip, the model names the direction itself.
Dolly away is the dolly-in clip played in reverse. This is exact, because nothing in the scene moves on its own.
Each class's speed is the midpoint of its grammar range: orbit sweep 42.5°, dolly end factor 0.6, pan 10°. Pan is the subtlest of the four.
All clips share one pose: distance 9 m, height 3.5 m, azimuth 0°, centred aim, gray checker ground, sky world, sun at 45°.
